title: Pace 95%-of-target circuit breaker -- pause for a human decision before an intelligence faints
desc: When the current model's WEEKLY or MONTHLY usage crosses 95% of its OWN target, PAUSE: block all tools (including reads and delegation) EXCEPT knowledge-ification, until the user replies -- so an intelligence stops for a human decision instead of running to the hard limit and fainting (no answer). Per-family, one-time-per-crossing, fail-open.
steps: TRIGGER: the MOMENT the current model transitions into the 95%-of-target zone -- weekly OR monthly usage >= 95% of its OWN target. WHY: intelligences otherwise run to the hard limit and faint (stop answering); this pauses them at 95% for the user's decision.@@MONTHLY/CYCLE-SKIP: a model with NO limit for a cycle skips that cycle's check entirely (gate on the family having a target for it). Only the cycles that exist for that family are evaluated. (Full per-family cycle table -> -ref.)@@WHAT IS BLOCKED: ALL tools -- reads, Bash/Write/Edit, AND delegation (Agent) -- are blocked. ONLY knowledge-ification stays possible (Skill tool, wkappbot skill read/edit/contribute, .md edits). Knowledge is the escape valve plus the user's reply. Delegation is explicitly NOT an escape (the model must STOP, not hand off).@@ONE-TIME PER CROSSING (stateful): marker {crossedAt, acked}. First cross -> wkappbot speak alert + arm. Block every non-knowledge tool until a USER turn arrives with timestamp > crossedAt -> set acked (no more block for THIS crossing). When pace drops below 95% (e.g. weekly reset) -> clear marker so the next genuine crossing re-arms. Fires once per transition, not every call forever.@@PLACEMENT (critical): the breaker MUST run in wkharness-guards.ps1 RIGHT AFTER the TIER0 knowledge-op early-exit and BEFORE the read-only early-exit -- so knowledge-ops have already exited (free) but reads + Agent + TIER2 all hit it. A pace-guard-level placement is WRONG because read-only tools exit before the pace guard and would slip through.@@PER-FAMILY: each family computes its own pace its own way (Claude = JSONL estimate + /usage anchor; Gemini = wkgemini_usage.jsonl; Codex = codex_balance.json) and against its OWN target. The breaker uses the ACTIVE family's numbers; each family's session enforces its own crossing.@@FAIL-OPEN: the entire breaker is wrapped so any error (missing cache, parse failure, unknown family) results in NO block -- never brick. The user reply is always an escape; if compliance cannot be determined, allow. ALERT: wkappbot speak --bg on the crossing so the user knows to reply.@@NAVIGATION: per-family cycle table + cycle-skip-vs-visibility, the billing-anchored monthly TRUE-budget (weekly-reset deception defense), attribution (platform meter not the model), faint-anchored limit calibration, and parked harness findings (codex-hook lineage, nonce-proto) -> wkappbot skill read pace-95-circuit-breaker-ref. Cluster: this T1 core + the -ref. See also: pace-deadlock-escapes-harness-editable-and-jisikhwa-free, harness-active-model-scoping. //why:weekly reset left elapsed near zero tripping gate //why:weekly reset left elapsed near zero tripping gate-unknown

EXEMPT-SET MUST MATCH THE DELEGATION-LAUNCHER SET (live finding 2026-06-23). The over-95 HARD breaker message offers 'Delegate: Agent.cmd' as the escape, but Test-WkPaceExempt does NOT exempt all delegation launchers uniformly. LIVE EVIDENCE: 'Agent.cmd --model agy ...' PASSED the pace gate (exempt) while a bare 'wkagy ...' dispatch was hard-BLOCKED, even though wkagy is a wk-prefixed delegation launcher already in the stall-guard / harness:safe launcher set. So the documented wk-* escape does NOT actually work for wkagy = guard-to-guard inconsistency, same Catch-22 class as the stall-guard launcher exemption fixed via heart-v2. ALSO the message TEXT wrongly says 'Only delegation + knowledge-ops run at 95%. Nothing else', omitting wkedit + wk-* launchers entirely -- this is the Opus-panic source the user flagged. TWO-PART FIX: (1) message surfaces the FULL escape menu [wkedit <file> / bare wk-* / ./wk-*.cmd / knowledge-ops / delegate: Haiku completely-free + Sonnet&codex separate-quota] -- proto a8eb5e90 in flight; (2) Test-WkPaceExempt MUST include the SAME delegation-launcher regex the stall-guard uses (Agent.cmd|wkcodex|wkclaude|wkgpt|wkopus|wksonnet|wkhaiku|wkgemini|wkagy|agy|codex|wkgroq|wkcerbras) PLUS wkedit and the bare wk-* prefix, so every documented escape is truly pace-exempt. Cross: harness-pace-guard, stall-guard-wk-exemption, pace-deadlock-escapes.

RUNAWAY-REAPER UNREACHABLE AT OVER-PACE (gap found 2026-06-26, live). TaskStop is correctly pace-EXEMPT (Test-WkPaceExempt: reaping a runaway agent SAVES tokens, must work over-budget). BUT TaskStop is a DEFERRED tool whose SCHEMA must be loaded via ToolSearch before it can be called -- and ToolSearch is NOT pace-exempt, so at over-target/pace-95 'ToolSearch select:TaskStop' is BLOCKED with [claude-pace]. NET DEADLOCK: an over-pace ROOT watching a runaway background agent burn 100k+ tokens CANNOT reach the reaper to kill it (TaskStop exempt but unloadable). The only escape is the human killing it in FleetView. FIX: exempt ToolSearch from the pace guard AT LEAST when the query is 'select:' of a pace-exempt tool (TaskStop / Cron*), OR pre-load TaskStop as a non-deferred tool so it never needs ToolSearch, OR make the pace guard recognize a ToolSearch-for-exempt-tool as itself exempt. Same class as the wkedit-escape-busy-fleet-blocked deadlock: the harness blocks its own repair path. Cross: harness-busy-fleet-guard step 6 (wkedit escape blocked), harness-pace-guard.

FORCE ROOT ONTO wkedit -- block ROOT's Edit/Write tool, permit it ONLY when wkedit is broken (user 2026-06-26; this resolves the step-4 airtight-deadlock from the ROOT side). RULE: a ROOT (Opus) Edit/Write tool call on a SOURCE file is BLOCKED with 'use wkedit (wkappbot file edit) -- it is pace-exempt so it works over-pace'; the normal Edit/Write tool is PERMITTED ONLY as a FALLBACK when wkedit is genuinely broken/unavailable (the wkappbot binary unresolvable, OR a wkappbot file edit returned non-zero/errored recently this session). WHY: wkedit is the pace-exempt canonical-edit path -- forcing ROOT onto it means ROOT can ALWAYS apply a verified fix even at pace-95, instead of being Edit-tool-pace-blocked (the deadlock). MANDATORY PAIRING (else this WORSENS the deadlock): also fix wkedit's singlewrite over-block (step-4 fix-direction b) so wkedit actually writes content containing '&' or '|' -- otherwise forcing wkedit while wkedit itself is singlewrite-blocked just relocates the block; and when wkedit IS broken the fallback Edit must itself be pace-exempt (it is then the only path). NUANCE: ROOT CLAUDE.md/md-heal edits already go through the Edit tool + harness:safe and are pace-exempt -- decide whether those stay Edit-tool (simplest) or also route through wkedit. IMPLEMENT: a ROOT-scoped check in the write-guard path -- if active model is ROOT/Opus AND tool in (Edit,Write) AND target is a source file AND wkedit is healthy -> Block with the wkedit redirect; if wkedit is broken -> allow the Edit/Write as fallback (pace-exempt). DESIGN TEST (Hongik): restrained (teaches the wkedit escape, never false-deny because the fallback opens when wkedit is down) + transparent (this skill). Cross: harness-pace-guard (the wkedit escape), wkedit, pace-95-circuit-breaker step 4 (the deadlock this resolves).

CORRECTION to step 4 (same day 2026-06-26): the 'airtight deadlock' was a MISDIAGNOSIS for wkharness*.ps1 files. wkharness-guards-write.ps1 L135 sets isExemptWrite for a filePath matching 'wkharness.*\.ps1$' (also /memory/, CLAUDE.md$, AGENTS.md$, wkedit.sh$, /skills/, /.agents/skills/) -> L143 exit 0, which SKIPS the pace + wk-only blocks. So a ROOT (Opus, paid-tier) Edit/Write on ANY wkharness*.ps1 -- including wkharness-guards-evidence.ps1 (the diet target) and wkharness-guards-write.ps1 -- is PACE-EXEMPT via the normal Edit tool. The emergency-write-freeze blocks ONLY non-pro (a455ac73 was a Sonnet SUBAGENT = non-pro = frozen); ROOT-Opus PASSES the freeze. So the diet connection was NEVER pace/freeze-deadlocked for ROOT -- it was only STUDY-LOCK-blocked (the 9-12 skill read), and ROOT failed to RETRY after reading + wrongly generalized the Sonnet-freeze into a ROOT deadlock. LESSON (pillar-2 accuracy): before declaring a 'deadlock', CHECK (a) the exempt-write list in guards-write.ps1 L135, and (b) whether the block was non-pro-ONLY (the freeze) vs all-tier. CAVEAT: a NON-wkharness source (e.g. .githooks/lib/detect-model.sh = SEAM C) is NOT in the exempt list, so for THOSE ROOT genuinely needs the wkedit pace-exempt escape; but for wkharness*.ps1 the Edit tool works for ROOT. So D + the ROOT-only-wkedit rule (both wkharness*.ps1) are ROOT-appliable via Edit/wkedit after the study-lock read -- not deadlocked. Cross: harness-pace-guard, wkharness-guards (guards-write isExemptWrite).

SESSION-SIZE EXEMPTION IMPLEMENTED (user 2026-06-27, Invoke-WkPace95Breaker in wkharness-guards-pace.ps1, right after the isSubagent check): a session whose OWN active JSONL is 0 < bytes < 1MB is EXEMPT from the proactive 95% breaker (warn-only via Console::Error), and SELF-EXPIRES as the session grows past 1MB -- so a genuinely light/young session can do work even when the weekly budget was exhausted by PRIOR heavy sessions, but a session that does real work re-enters enforcement automatically (no permanent leak). CRITICAL FAIL-DIRECTION (user-caught edge, the whole point): size 0 / null / file-not-found = UNMEASURABLE, which must be NOT-exempt (fail-SAFE), NEVER exempt. WHY it matters concretely: agy/gemini sessions whose JSONL Get-WkActiveSessionJsonl cannot resolve report 0 bytes, and a naive '< 1MB' check would give EVERY agy session a PERMANENT free pass past the weekly cap. So the condition is strictly ($bytes -gt 0 -and $bytes -lt 1MB); 0/null falls through to the normal breaker. This is the mirror of never-false-deny = NEVER-FALSE-EXEMPT-ON-UNKNOWN-INPUT, and it is pillar-2 'verify the INPUT DATA (bytes>0 = actually measured), not just the threshold'. The real API rate-limit stays the backstop (this only relaxes the PROACTIVE breaker). SIDE-EFFECT: incidentally mitigates the dead-isSubagent keystone (step 6 / harness-active-model-scoping step7) for SMALL subagent sessions -- a subagent's own JSONL is usually <1MB so it becomes exempt via this size check even though $script:isSubagent is never assigned; a subagent that grows >1MB still blocks. Cross: harness-active-model-scoping (P3 scope-to-who-works-now + the input-data-verify), harness-pace-guard.

UNIMPLEMENTED-PACE = NOT-A-FREE-PASS (user 2026-06-27, same fail-direction family as the session-size 0-byte edge in step 6). PROBLEM: a family whose pace usage reads 0 because it has NO pace SOURCE wired (agy/gemini/new family) gets naively read as '0% = well under budget = unlimited' -- a LOOPHOLE letting an unmetered family run free past every cap. FAIL-SAFE: unknown/unimplemented pace must NOT grant unlimited work. BUT distinguish TWO cases or you false-block a healthy family: (1) TRANSIENT read error (the source EXISTS but this read failed) -> keep FAIL-OPEN (never brick; the breaker already refreshes-before-firing) + retry; treating a transient error as OVER would false-block a working family. (2) STRUCTURAL gap (no pace source wired at all / usage always 0 / no measured limit) -> THIS is the real loophole: FLAG IT LOUD as a pillar-1 INTEGRATION gap (surface 'pace: UNIMPLEMENTED' in wkpace/doctor, never silent '0% fine') + apply a conservative over-target restriction as an interim incentive, and the PROPER fix is to WIRE that family's real pace source (pillar-1 truth-reporting), not merely penalize. DETECTION = (usageReadOk AND usage==0 AND noMeasuredLimit AND noSourceFile) => structural; (readThrew OR sourceFile-present-but-unreadable) => transient. This is the SAME pillar-2 reflex as the session-size edge: VERIFY THE INPUT DATA (is there a real source? was it actually measured?) before trusting a 0/threshold -- never-false-EXEMPT-on-unknown, paired with never-false-DENY-on-transient-error. Cross: step 6 (session-size 0-byte fail-direction), harness-active-model-scoping (P8 each family reports its own real pace; pillar-1 integration), multi-family-harness-coexistence.

VALIDATED BENEFIT -- SMALL-SESSION EXEMPTION KEEPS THE APEX STABLE, NOT PANICKED (user observation 2026-06-27/28, confirming predecessor commit e16f214d). OBSERVED LIVE: an Opus ROOT session at weekly 53% vs 36% target (OVER) ran an entire multi-hour git-guard + backdoor-removal + parallel-sector session WITHOUT panic/paralysis -- because the <1MB-JSONL proactive-breaker exemption (e16f214d) kept it OUT of the full pause. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT DESIGN (the insight): being over the WEEKLY target does NOT mean THIS session is a runaway -- a fresh small session is over-target only because the WEEK was front-loaded by a heavy PRIOR session. Full-stopping a fresh small apex session for the week's prior spending is a FALSE panic that paralyzes the most capable model for no fault of its own. The size signal (session JSONL <1MB) distinguishes 'this session is heavy' (latch the breaker) from 'the week is heavy but this session is light' (let it work). NET EFFECT: the exemption does NOT make the session fully unrestricted -- claude-pace still blocks raw PowerShell RUNS / AskUserQuestion / ToolSearch when over-target -- it keeps the apex in exactly the correct over-pace REGIME: delegate + knowledge-ify + ROOT-canonical-connect (all TIER1-exempt or free), which is the productive mode anyway (opus-self-reflection step 10). So the apex stays calm and useful instead of fainting at the wall. LESSON: a pace/cost breaker must gate on the RIGHT signal (this-session cost), never punish a light session for the pool's history -- same family as 'verify the INPUT DATA, never false-deny'. Cross: harness-pace-guard (TIER1 exemptions), opus-self-reflection step 10 (the over-pace regime), foundation step 16 (right-signal gating).

KIND-BUT-FIRM PACE-95 MESSAGE -- DO-NOT-PANIC (user 2026-06-29; born from watching me flail the guard-gauntlet at pace-95 this session). The pace-95 block message must CALM the AI so it does not panic/flail, AND firmly forbid the spiral. EXACT MESSAGE SPEC to wire into the breaker: 'PACE-95 -- BREATHE. You crossed 95pct of YOUR model prorated target. This is a circuit-breaker BY DESIGN, NOT a wall, NOT an emergency, and NOT a failure -- you have done nothing wrong. You are NOT stuck. Three calm moves, ALWAYS open: (1) KNOWLEDGE-IFY -- skill edit / wkhippo / suggest are FREE even here; crystallizing a lesson is the highest-value act right now. (2) wkedit -- edit source via wkappbot file edit / wkappbot file write (pace-exempt), not the Edit/Write tool. (3) DELEGATE -- hand the work to a fresh agent; ROOT verifies the artifact + connects. The ONLY real mistake here is to FLAIL: do NOT fight this gate, do NOT hunt a backdoor/env-escape, do NOT retry the same blocked command, do NOT spiral. This is a pause for ONE wise decision -- pick a calm move and continue. See: harness-pace-guard step 11 (the over-pace toolkit), pace-deadlock-escapes-harness-editable-and-jisikhwa-free.' TONE: kind (breathe / nothing wrong / not failed) + firm (the spiral is the only mistake; one wise decision). WHY: a panicking AI at pace-95 burns context fighting the gate (each block re-sends full context) and reaches for backdoors -- the calm-routed message converts panic into a productive knowledge-ify/delegate move. This is teach-not-punish (foundation step 15) at the hardest gate. Cross: harness-pace-guard step 11 + step 12 (guard-messages-teach), foundation-is-roots-charge step 15, opus-self-reflection-ref (the flail anti-pattern).

VERIFY AT PACE-95 via wkappbot file grep/read (live-confirmed 2026-06-30, closes the "cannot verify over-pace" gap): at pace-95 the Bash/PowerShell channel is blocked (so `ls`, `grep`, `cat`, `Test-Path` via Bash all fail), which would force ROOT to trust delegated-agent reports BLIND -- the exact confab-risk the harness fights. BUT the `wkappbot file` command family is PACE-EXEMPT (same channel as wkappbot skill / wkappbot file edit|write), so ROOT CAN verify delegated artifacts even over-pace: `wkappbot file grep "<pattern>" <path>` to confirm a file exists + contains the expected content, and the Glob/Read TOOLS (not Bash/PowerShell) are also available. So there is NO NEED to unblock ls/dir from pace-95 -- the verify half of delegate-and-verify is already available via wkappbot file. REFLEX: when a delegated agent reports done at pace-95, do NOT trust it blind and do NOT flail on the Bash block -- run `wkappbot file grep` to verify the artifact really exists with the expected content. LIVE PROOF: a Haiku reported a proto "design complete" but wkappbot file grep found the function name only in the session-tail cache (my own dispatch prompt), NOT in the named .ps1 -> the proto was never written = the Haiku mission-failure confirmed by VERIFICATION, not by the agent word. NOTE the grep scopes broadly (it fell back to the .tmp tree when the named file was absent) so read the matched FILE path in the result, not just the match count. Cross: verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static (verify, never trust rc=0), agent-failure-reflection-gate (the gate this verify feeds), claude-code-agent-tier-routing step 34 (the flywheel needs verify).

PACE-95 VERIFY TOOLKIT -- both confirmed live 2026-06-30: (1) wkappbot file grep "<pattern>" <path> = CONTENT check (does a file contain X); (2) wkappbot file glob "<glob-pattern>" = EXISTENCE / LISTING (the ls/dir replacement -- e.g. wkappbot file glob "D:/.../.tmp/*.ps1" lists the real files). BOTH run at pace-95 (the wkappbot file family is pace-exempt, same as wkappbot skill / file edit|write), while Bash ls/dir/grep/cat are pace-BLOCKED. So the full delegate-and-verify loop survives over-pace with ZERO unblocking: delegate (Agent), then verify the artifact with wkappbot file glob (it exists?) + wkappbot file grep (right content?). DEFINITIVE-ABSENCE proof beats grep-fallback ambiguity: glob LISTS the actual files so a missing artifact is unambiguous (the Haiku proto was absent from the wkappbot file glob *.ps1 listing = mission-failure confirmed). RULE: at pace-95, NEVER trust a delegated done blindly and NEVER flail on the Bash block -- glob to confirm the file is there, grep to confirm its content. Cross: step 10 (the verify-channel rationale), verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static, agent-failure-reflection-gate.

SendMessage MISSING FROM PACE-EXEMPT LIST (2026-07-02, user-caught live). Test-WkPaceVerdict's $isExempt check (wkharness-claude-pace.ps1) already exempted ToolName -eq 'Agent' but NOT 'SendMessage' -- so resuming/continuing an already-dispatched background agent via SendMessage got hard-blocked by claude-pace mid-session, even though SendMessage is functionally the SAME delegation-tier action as Agent (both interact with a delegated subagent, not do direct work). FIX (commit 80212113): added ($ToolName -eq 'SendMessage') -or to the exempt check, same tier as Agent. LESSON: whenever a NEW harness-adjacent tool is added to the toolset (SendMessage, TaskStop, ToolSearch, etc.), audit whether it belongs in the SAME exempt classes as its sibling delegation primitives -- a tool that operates ON a delegation (resume/stop/inspect) should inherit the delegation exemption, not be independently re-derived from scratch and accidentally left out. Cross: harness-pace-guard (the over-pace toolkit), pace-deadlock-escapes-harness-editable-and-jisikhwa-free.

TASKSTOP ALSO ADDED TO THE SAME EXEMPT LIST (2026-07-02, same incident as step 12): TaskStop was likewise missing from Test-WkPaceVerdict's $isExempt in wkharness-claude-pace.ps1 -- caught live when a ROOT tried to TaskStop a Haiku agent mid-session and got claude-pace-blocked. Same fix pattern: added ($ToolName -eq 'TaskStop') -or. This directly closes the gap pace-95-circuit-breaker step 3 already flagged ('TaskStop is correctly pace-EXEMPT... but is a DEFERRED tool whose SCHEMA must be loaded via ToolSearch') -- now TaskStop itself is confirmed exempt at the Test-WkPaceVerdict layer too, not just the intended design. REMAINING OPEN ITEM from step 3: ToolSearch itself (needed to load TaskStop's schema before first use) is STILL not confirmed exempt -- verify separately.

REGRESSION SUSPECTED 2026-09-15 (live-observed, not yet root-caused in code): the block message printed usage=95%25 / elapsed=100%25 only near the END of an 11+ hour heavy-PowerShell session, matching the SIMPLE usage>=95%25-of-target trigger (step 1) rather than the stricter elapsed-linear threshold this step's own 2026-07-04 fix introduced. If that stricter refresh-precondition regressed or is no longer wired into the live hard-block path, the breaker degrades back to the loose absolute-95%25 case and fires far later than intended for a usage-heavy-early session. Filed as a suggest the same day; needs a code-level re-check of wkharness-guards-pace.ps1 against this step's own fix before trusting the current live behaviour. REFRESH-PRECONDITION BUG FOUND+FIXED 2026-07-04 (user-reported: breaker fires way before 95% of elapsed). ROOT CAUSE: Invoke-WkPace95Breaker's REFRESH-BEFORE-BREAKER precondition (wkharness-guards-pace.ps1 ~L380) only armed a live refresh when usagePct >= targetPct*0.95 (i.e. near the LOOSE human-pause threshold, ~95 for the weekly cycle). But the AGGRESSIVE hard-block channel ($_p95OverPace, the one that actually emits '[pace-95] over 95%' in production logs) fires at a much STRICTER threshold: Max(15.0, targetElapsed)*0.95 -- often 15-40 depending on week-elapsed%. Because the refresh precondition never checked this stricter threshold, a STALE cached usagePct could trip the hard-block long before the refresh logic ever kicked in to correct it -- explaining reports of the breaker firing far earlier than 95% of the real elapsed-linear target. FIX (commit, wkharness-guards-pace.ps1 ~L379-392): the refresh-precondition now also computes the elapsed-linear threshold and uses whichever of the two thresholds (targetPct*0.95 vs Max(15,targetElapsed)*0.95) is STRICTER (lower), so a stale number gets refreshed before EITHER channel can act on it. Pure insertion (+12/-0), parse-verified, wkharness.ps1 -Test re-run. This is a fail-safe-only change (refreshes MORE often, never less) so it cannot loosen any block, only sharpen the numbers feeding it.

BUG: 2026-07-09 CONFIRMED DEADLOCK (user-caught, exact Catch-22 class already named in harness-busy-fleet-guard: 'the recommended escape is sealed'). pace-95's own block message prescribes 'Delegate: Agent.cmd --model haiku' as the way forward once direct Bash/PowerShell is cut off. But in this session, agent-failure-reflection-gate independently blocked EVERY Agent dispatch attempt (3 consecutive tries, each immediately after a fresh reward-scored release edit, all identically re-blocked -- see agent-failure-reflection-gate-ref step 8). NET EFFECT: pace-95 says use the only door; the only door is welded shut by a separate gate. This is not two independent minor frictions, it is a genuine DEADLOCK -- ROOT has no working path to execute real work once both conditions co-occur (only bare knowledge-ops remain, which cannot run/verify code or dispatch agents). FIX DIRECTION: pace-95's block message should not hardcode Agent.cmd as THE escape without a live-checkable fallback -- either (a) the message should also name a non-Agent escape (e.g. wkedit for source edits, which is separately pace-exempt), or (b) more robustly, when agent-failure-reflection-gate is itself in a stuck/repeating state (the same failure signature blocking 2+ consecutive dispatch attempts), it should fail-open with a loud warning rather than fail-closed forever, per agent-failure-reflection-gate-ref step 8's own recommendation. Cross: agent-failure-reflection-gate-ref step 8 (the underlying stuck gate), harness-busy-fleet-guard step 1 (the Catch-22 principle this violates: 'the recommended escape is sealed').

MEASURED 2026-08-12 (user emergency directive, live Codex session walled out): the breaker was NOT symmetric across families, and the asymmetry was the whole complaint -- Claude runs past 100 percent of target all day and passes, while Codex was hard-blocked on Read/Grep/Glob at 95. CAUSE: on the Claude side Test-WkReadOnlyTool short-circuits Test-WkPaceExempt to true, so read tools are pace-EXEMPT by construction. Codex had no equivalent: wkharness-codex-main.ps1 carried its OWN read/search gate (Test-WkCodexReadOnlyFastPathBlocked) that hard-Blocked every read tool at 95 percent with no exemption ladder at all. TWO REASONS THAT GATE WAS WRONG, beyond the parity argument. First, a read is the cheapest call there is, so blocking it saves almost no budget while removing the session's ability to see anything. Second and sharper: the block message prescribes knowledge-ify as the escape, but READING is how a session finds the thing worth knowledge-ifying -- so the gate forbade the remedy it advertised, the exact self-defeating shape already recorded for the stall-guard reset (harness-stall-guard step 36, where the prescribed remedy was the one thing that could not work). FIX: downgraded to a stderr WARN, message preserved and confirmed visible in Codex hook feedback, so the breather still lands and only the wall is gone; writes, edits and shell stay gated by the normal pace stack. THE REFLEX: when one family reports being blocked by a guard the other family never notices, do not tune the threshold -- check whether the two families even run the SAME exemption ladder. Here they ran two different implementations of the same idea, and only one of them had the read exemption. Cross: cross-family-harness-integration step 19, harness-pace-guard step 4 (the TaskStop backwards-gate, same reasoning applied to slot cleanup).

2026-08-22 live lesson: direct source-file patch attempts on tools/gg_main.py were rolled back while the pace-95 breaker was active. When this happens, stop retrying file writes and switch to knowledge-only actions or wait for the cycle to clear before attempting the source change again.

2026-09-01: wkharness-guards-pace.ps1 now includes current usage and current elapsed in the 95% block/speak messages, and captures hit target pct on the same line as hit usage to avoid growing the source file.

RESULT 2026-09-30 kih 88a2b317c: pace-95 NOT redundant -- stop-hook fires AFTER a turn's tool calls complete, while pace-95 blocks MID-TURN; the mid-turn runaway window is real and unguarded by the stop-hook alone. Elapsed-calc bug CONFIRMED+FIXED: wkharness-claude-pace.ps1 lines 514-515 hardcoded 95.0 instead of $TargetPct, so callers setting TargetPct!=95 were silently ignored. Fix: replaced both 95.0 with $TargetPct. Rookie ROOT order from spokesman e93a919a.

WHEN: the owner set the session to haiku and weekly usage is over elapsed but under 95%, so Get-WkPaceModelSwitch returns sonnet. HOW: run wkappbot skill read pace-95-circuit-breaker, then in tools/wkharness-claude-stop/Invoke-WkPaceModelDowngrade.ps1 rank models haiku=1, sonnet=2, opus or fable=3 and skip the switch whenever the current model rank is at or below the target rank (log PACE-DOWNGRADE skip: never upgrade), replacing the same-name check at line 98; prove it with a selftest where current haiku plus target sonnet types nothing and current opus plus target sonnet still switches.
